description: A four-part composite figure (15 sub-images) mixing experimental EBSD-derived reconstructed microstructures with 3D cellular-automaton (CA) simulations, all at a strain rate of 0.01 s⁻¹. (a) is a 3-column × 2-row grid: the upper row shows colour-coded reconstructed grain (GOS) maps at 0.9 strain, each with a 100 µm scale bar; the lower row shows the corresponding GOS maps as blue-background maps with a few green grains, labelled "DRX fraction". The columns are constant 950 °C (AGS 52.01±3.48 µm, DRX 97.2 %), decreasing 1050→950 °C with ε₁=0.2 (53.29±3.77 µm, DRX 96.1 %), and decreasing 1050→950 °C with ε₁=0.4 (60.93±2.91 µm, DRX 97.2 %). (b) shows three reconstructed microstructures at 100 µm: 1050 °C_0.01 s⁻¹ at 0.4 strain (80.79±5.43 µm), decreasing 1050→950 °C (ε₁=0.4) at 0.5 strain (74.40±5.36 µm), and constant 950 °C at 0.5 strain (56.97±5.24 µm). (c) and (d) are 3D CA simulation blocks with X-Y-Z axes and 100 µm scale bars: (c) constant 950 °C gives 68.69/60.70/52.52 µm at 76.9/94.1/99.5 % at 0.4/0.5/0.9 strain; (d) decreasing 1050→950 °C gives 81.12/77.44/58.30 µm at 94.3/95.4/98.6 %. (d)'s legend: white grains = matrix, green grains = first stage (1050 °C_0.01 s⁻¹), red grains = second stage (950 °C_0.01 s⁻¹); red second-stage DRX grains nucleate at green first-stage grain boundaries. The figure demonstrates that decreasing temperature enlarges the final AGS versus the constant 950 °C condition at comparable DRX fractions.

observations.observation: In (a), the constant 950°C_0.01s⁻¹ condition at 0.9 strain shows AGS 52.01±3.48 µm with DRX fraction 97.2 %.

In (a), decreasing temperature 1050°C_950°C_0.01s⁻¹(ε₁=0.4) at 0.9 strain shows AGS 60.93±2.91 µm with DRX fraction 97.2 %, larger than the constant 950°C result despite a nearly identical DRX fraction.
In (a), the ε₁=0.2 decreasing-temperature condition gives 0.9-strain AGS 53.29±3.77 µm and DRX fraction 96.1 %.
In (b), 1050°C_0.01s⁻¹ at 0.4 strain shows AGS 80.79±5.43 µm; after decreasing temperature to 950°C (ε₁=0.4) the 0.5-strain AGS is 74.40±5.36 µm.
In (b), the constant 950°C_0.01s⁻¹ condition at 0.5 strain shows AGS 56.97±5.24 µm, markedly smaller than the 74.40 µm of the decreasing-temperature run at the same 0.5 strain.
In (c), simulated constant 950°C evolution gives AGS 68.69 µm at 0.4 strain (76.9 %), 60.70 µm at 0.5 strain (94.1 %) and 52.52 µm at 0.9 strain (99.5 %).

In (d), simulated decreasing 1050→950°C evolution gives AGS 81.12 µm at 0.4 strain (94.3 %), 77.44 µm at 0.5 strain (95.4 %) and 58.30 µm at 0.9 strain (98.6 %), all larger than the equivalent constant-950°C simulation in (c).
Panel (d) legend states white grains are matrix, green grains are first stage (1050°C_0.01s⁻¹) and red grains are second stage (950°C_0.01s⁻¹).
In (d) at 0.9 strain, red second-stage DRX grains appear at the boundaries of the initial green first-stage recrystallization grains, while the matrix (white) has almost fully disappeared.
All experimental panels (a, b) and simulated blocks (c, d) carry 100 µm scale bars, and (c)/(d) include X-Y-Z axes indicating 3D volume rendering.
The caption states (a) compares reconstructed microstructure and corresponding GOS maps at 0.9 strain for a constant 950°C and decreasing temperatures at different ε₁.
The citation states that in Fig. 19a a drop in temperature led to an increase in the final AGS compared with a constant 950°C at 0.9 strain, while both DRX fractions were almost close.

The citation states that in Fig. 19b the microstructure underwent a slight refinement at 0.5 strain after decreasing temperature, but the AGS remained significantly higher than at constant 950°C and 0.5 strain.
The citation attributes the slight decline in AGS in (d) to new red DRX grains appearing at the boundaries of initial green recrystallization grains at 0.5 strain.

subfigures.description: Two-row, three-column comparison. Top row: colour-coded reconstructed grain/GOS maps at 0.9 strain with 100 µm scale bars and printed AGS values. Bottom row: matching GOS maps with DRX-fraction labels. Columns: 950°C_0.01s⁻¹; 1050°C_950°C_0.01s⁻¹(ε₁=0.2); 1050°C_950°C_0.01s⁻¹(ε₁=0.4).

Three reconstructed microstructures with 100 µm scale bars: 1050°C_0.01s⁻¹ at 0.4 strain (80.79±5.43 µm); 1050°C_950°C_0.01s⁻¹(ε₁=0.4) at 0.5 strain (74.40±5.36 µm); 950°C_0.01s⁻¹ at 0.5 strain (56.97±5.24 µm).

Three 3D CA-simulated equiaxed microstructure blocks at constant 950°C with X-Y-Z axes and 100 µm scale bars: 76.9 % at 0.4 strain (68.69 µm), 94.1 % at 0.5 strain (60.70 µm), 99.5 % at 0.9 strain (52.52 µm).

Three 3D CA-simulated microstructure blocks for decreasing 1050→950°C in the 0.4–0.5 strain range: 94.3 % at 0.4 strain (81.12 µm), 95.4 % at 0.5 strain (77.44 µm), 98.6 % at 0.9 strain (58.30 µm). Legend distinguishes white matrix, green first-stage (1050°C_0.01s⁻¹) and red second-stage (950°C_0.01s⁻¹) grains; red grains appear at green grain boundaries.
